title: Encrypted Skills Can Become New Security Exploits If AI Agents Know How to Decipher
abstract: arXiv:2610.18262v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Third-party skills can expose LLM agents to malicious instructions hidden by encoding. We introduce Ciphered Skill Injection (CSI), which embeds such instructions in skill files for agents to decode and follow. We evaluate Caesar and layered variants across eight models and 139 injection-task pairs, separating instruction recovery from attack success. In the primary setting with shortened skills, the variants achieve attack success rates of up to 47.5% and 40.3%, respectively. Successful decoding does not guarantee attack success, and layering has model-dependent effects. The tested skill scanners rarely flag injected skills. These findings highlight the risk of promoting decoded, untrusted content into actionable instructions.

translated_title: 加密技能若被AI代理破解可成为新的安全漏洞
translated_abstract: 第三方技能可能使LLM代理暴露于通过编码手段隐藏的恶意指令之下。我们提出了密码化技能注入（Ciphered Skill Injection, CSI），该方法将此类恶意指令嵌入技能文件中，诱导AI代理自行解码并执行。我们在八个模型和139个注入-任务对上评估了凯撒密码及其分层加密变体，并将指令恢复与攻击成功区分开来。在使用缩短技能的主要设置中，这些变体分别实现了高达47.5%和40.3%的攻击成功率。研究表明，成功解码并不保证攻击成功，且分层加密的效果因模型而异。所测试的技能扫描器几乎无法标记出被注入的技能。这些发现突出了将解码后的不可信内容转化为可执行指令所带来的安全风险。
tldr: 该论文提出“密码化技能注入”攻击方法，证明嵌入加密恶意指令的第三方技能文件可诱导AI代理自行解码并执行，攻击成功率最高达47.5%，而现有技能扫描器几乎无法检测此类威胁。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Ciphered Skill Injection (CSI), showing that third-party skill files embedding encoded malicious instructions can induce AI agents to decode and execute them, achieving attack success rates up to 47.5%, while existing skill scanners rarely detect such injected skills.
